source_text: Καὶ ἐκπέπληγμαι δὲ, ὁπότ᾽ ἂν ἀπίδω οἷα καὶ ὅσα εἰς βλάβην τῶν πέλας ἄνθρωποι ἐπιτετηδεύκασιν. Ἐπίσταμαι δὲ προαναρπαζομένους ἐνθένδε τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς καὶ γινομένους ἐκ ποδῶν, ἄνθ᾽ ὧν ἑαυτοὺς ματαιότητι δεδώκεσαν. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ οὐκ ἐφ᾽ ἁπάντων μετέρχεται ἡ τοῦ Θεοῦ πρόνοια ὀξέως διὰ τὴν πολλὴν ἀνεξικακίαν, οὐδὲ παραυτίκα τιμωρεῖται ἐπὶ ταῖς πλημμελείαις, τούτου χάριν οἴεται δεῖν ὁ πονηρὸς ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτάνειν ἐπὶ πλεῖον, ὡς ἀθῶος ἀπαλλάξων· οὐ συνιεὶς, ὅτι καὶ μετὰ πάμπολυν χρόνον ἀδικήσας οὐ λήσεται· ἀγαθόν γε μὴν μέγιστον, εὐλαβεῖσθαι Θεόν· οὗπερ ἀσεβὴς ἐκπεσὼν, οὐ πολὺν χρόνον τῇ ἑαυτοῦ μωρίᾳ καταχρήσεται. Χειρίστη δὲ καὶ ἐψευσμένη δόξα ἀνθρώπους ἐπινέμεται πολλάκις, περί τε δικαίων καὶ ἀδίκων. Ὑπολαμβάνουσι γὰρ περὶ ἑκατέρων τἀναντία· καὶ δίκαιός γε τὶς ὢν, οὐ τοιοῦτος ἔδοξε· καὶ πάλιν ἀσεβὴς, ἔμφρων ἐνομίσθη. Ταύτην ἔγωγε τὴν πλάνην χαλεπὴν ἐν τοῖς μάλιστα τίθεμαι.
thought_title: Slow punishment emboldens sinners and people misjudge righteous and wicked
orientation: Gregory continues paraphrasing Solomon on how coming judgment bears on human life.
pass_a_gloss: And I have been struck with amazement, whenever I look at what sort and how many things men have practiced for harm to their neighbors. But I know that the impious are being snatched away beforehand from here and are being made out of the way, in return for which things they have given themselves to emptiness. For since the providence of God does not come swiftly upon all things because of its great forbearance, nor is punishment inflicted at once for the offenses, for this reason the evil man thinks it right to sin still more, as one who will escape unpunished; not understanding that even having acted unjustly for a very long time he will not escape notice; but indeed the greatest good is to revere God; from which having fallen away, the impious man will not indulge his own folly for much time. But a worst and falsified opinion spreads among men often, concerning both righteous and unrighteous. For they suppose opposite things concerning each of the two; and someone being righteous did not seem such; and again an impious man was deemed sensible. This error I myself place among the most grievous.

pass_b_english: I am amazed whenever I look at the kinds of harm people devise against their neighbors, and how much of it. I know that the wicked are snatched away from here before their time and cleared out of the way, because they gave themselves over to emptiness.

God’s providence does not come swiftly upon everything, because He is greatly forbearing, and offenses are not punished at once (Ecclesiastes 8:11). For this reason the wicked man thinks he ought to go on sinning, as one who will escape unpunished. He does not understand that even when he has done wrong for a very long time, he will not escape notice. The greatest good is to fear God (Ecclesiastes 8:12). Once the impious man has fallen away from that fear, he will not indulge his own folly for long.

A worst and falsified opinion often spreads among people about the just and the unjust (Ecclesiastes 8:14). They assume the opposite about each sort. A man who is just is not thought to be so, while a man who is impious is thought wise. I count this delusion among the most grievous of all.

last_rejected.quote: even when he has done wrong for a very long time, he will not escape notice
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ μετὰ πάμπολυν χρόνον ἀδικήσας οὐ λήσεται
last_rejected.why: μετὰ πάμπολυν χρόνον means after a long delay, not that the wrongdoing itself lasted long.
last_rejected.fix: He does not understand that even after a very long time, the one who has done wrong will not escape notice.
last_rejected.ruling: μετὰ πάμπολυν χρόνον ἀδικήσας is 'having done wrong after a very long time'; the English 'even when he has done wrong for a very long time' is a loose but close rendering. The point, that he will not escape notice, is kept.
